findings.evidence:
In this commit, `PlanBuilder.buildAdmin` returns early for plugin ops and bypasses the SUPER visitInfo append: `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:1445-1448` returns `&AdminPlugins{...}` directly, while `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:1476-1478` is the only place that appends `mysql.SuperPriv` for admin statements.
Privilege enforcement in planning depends on collected visitInfo: `pkg/planner/optimize.go:474-479` calls `core.CheckPrivilege(..., builder.GetVisitInfo())`.
Executor path has no additional privilege guard: `pkg/executor/admin_plugins.go:35-53` executes `plugin.ChangeDisableFlagAndFlush(...)` without verification.
findings.fix: Re-introduce a privilege requirement for `ADMIN PLUGINS ENABLE/DISABLE` (at least `mysql.SuperPriv`) even if other admin commands are exempt. Minimal change: don’t early-return for `ast.AdminPluginEnable/Disable`; instead assign `ret = &AdminPlugins{...}` so the existing `appendVisitInfo(mysql.SuperPriv, ...)` at the end of `buildAdmin` applies. Alternatively, explicitly append an appropriate dynamic privilege / SUPER visitInfo before the early return.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user (even with no granted privileges) can execute `ADMIN PLUGINS ENABLE/DISABLE` and toggle plugin state cluster-wide via etcd flush, potentially disabling audit/security/observability plugins or otherwise changing runtime behavior without authorization.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed as of `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` still has early returns for `ast.AdminPluginEnable/Disable`, and `upstream/master:pkg/executor/admin_plugins.go` still has no privilege checks.
findings.verify: Add/restore a privilege test that does not depend on any plugin being installed: create a user with no SUPER, run `ADMIN PLUGINS DISABLE audit`, and assert it fails at privilege-check time (e.g. error 8121 for `Super`). Also assert a SUPER user passes privilege check (execution may still error if the plugin is not present, but it must not fail with privilege error).
findings.what: Privilege bypass: `ADMIN PLUGINS ENABLE/DISABLE` no longer requires `SUPER` because `buildAdmin` returns before appending the `mysql.SuperPriv` visitInfo, and the executor doesn’t enforce privileges either.

subject: *: Revert "add super privilege check for some admin commands (#51497)" (#51938)
summary: This revert changes `buildAdmin` to early-return for several `ADMIN ...` statement types, skipping the previously-unconditional `mysql.SuperPriv` visitInfo append. As a result, those admin commands (notably `ADMIN PLUGINS ENABLE/DISABLE`) lose SUPER privilege enforcement at planning time.
